teams.heading: Fiji Rugby launches limited-edition Coca-Cola cans featuring Sevens campaign moments
teams.body: Fiji Rugby and Coca-Cola Europacific Partners have unveiled a new collection of limited-edition cans and bottles to honour the national men’s sevens team. The series celebrates eight key moments from the 2025 Hong Kong and Singapore tournaments, with the launch event hosted at Albert Park in Suva. Fiji Rugby Commercial Director Tevita Tuiloa described the initiative as a way to recognise the shared relationship between the sport and the Fijian community, noting the profound impact of rugby on villages and schools nationwide.

teams.heading: Joe Carpenter eyes England return by targeting duel with George Furbank
teams.body: Sale full-back Joe Carpenter is hoping to reignite his international career by outperforming George Furbank during this weekend’s Premiership action. Carpenter, who has not played for England since July 2025, has benefited from a full pre-season to focus on his attacking game. “It would be nice to have a very good performance against them and against that England competition,” Carpenter said. While currently outside of Steve Borthwick’s selection, he remains hopeful of forcing his way into the setup for the upcoming November internationals.

teams.heading: Victor Wembanyama trains with Provence Rugby to improve physical conditioning
teams.body: NBA superstar Victor Wembanyama has revealed he spent part of his off-season training with French second-tier side Provence. The 22-year-old sought to develop his movement patterns and strength, participating in line-out drills and taking part in team sessions. Wembanyama, who joined team-mate Harrison Barnes for the visit, praised the camaraderie of the squad. He noted that the experience was deeply inspiring, stating, "It was a great experience, seeing the team spirit they have over there."

teams.heading: Eddie O’Sullivan warns of Springbok power after Leinster’s scrum struggle
teams.body: Former Ireland head coach Eddie O’Sullivan has highlighted the physical dominance of the South African scrum as a major challenge for Andy Farrell’s side ahead of their meeting next month. Following Leinster’s recent difficulties against the Sharks, where they conceded eight scrum penalties, O’Sullivan noted that such power is currently a widespread issue across international rugby. He argued that the Springboks’ ability to dominate physically represents a significant hurdle for every nation facing them, describing their set-piece as "frightening to watch."

teams.heading: Italy prepare for South Africa return to the Allianz Stadium
teams.body: Top-level international rugby returns to Turin next month as Italy prepare to host reigning world champions South Africa. The Allianz Stadium serves as the venue for this Nations Championship encounter, marking the third consecutive year the stadium has hosted an international test match. Italy will be aiming to improve upon their result against the Springboks in their previous meeting, which saw the side fall to a 32-14 defeat during the 2025 international friendlies.

teams.heading: Scottish Rugby and Macron launch new vintage-inspired Archive Collection range
teams.body: Scottish Rugby has collaborated with Macron to release The Archive Collection, a new range of kit designs that reinterpret classic styles from the 1990s and early 2000s. The project, which officially launched on Thursday, features current Scotland stars including Ewan Ashman, Jamie Dobie, Pierre Schoeman, and Rory Sutherland alongside several legends of the game. According to the governing body, the collection aims to connect different generations of fans by blending heritage details with modern design codes.

teams.heading: Shaun Edwards joins Felipe Contepomi’s Argentina staff for World Cup push
teams.body: World-renowned defence coach Shaun Edwards has been appointed to the Argentina backroom staff, signing a deal that runs until the conclusion of the 2027 Rugby World Cup in Australia. After finalising his consultancy with the Red Roses on 30 October, the 59-year-old will join head coach Felipe Contepomi’s team ahead of the upcoming Nations Championship fixtures. “I’m thrilled to be joining Felipe Contepomi, his coaching staff, and the Argentinian team,” Edwards said of his new role.

teams.heading: Australia suffer heavy defeat as All Blacks retain the Bledisloe Cup
teams.body: The Wallabies' challenge for the Bledisloe Cup ended in a 50-19 defeat at Eden Park, extending Australia's winless streak at the venue to 40 years. Despite leading 17-14 at half-time, Australia conceded 26 consecutive second-half points to the hosts. Head coach Les Kiss noted the side struggled against the aerial dominance of the All Blacks. The loss, which forces Australia to regroup for the Sydney rematch, also saw centre Len Ikitau depart the field with a concussion.

teams.heading: Japan Rugby Football Union outlines future social values at forum
teams.body: The Japan Rugby Football Union held its 100th Anniversary Gratitude and Future Forum this week, shifting focus from on-field performance to the long-term societal impact of the sport. The online event explored how core values like the spirit of 'No Side', respect for diversity, and the 'One Team' philosophy can be utilised to address social change. Top executives and stakeholders discussed the union’s mid-term strategic plan, aiming to redefine rugby’s role in Japan beyond the professional and international game.

teams.heading: Dave Rennie prioritises accountability with aggressive changes to All Blacks squad
teams.body: Former hooker James Parsons has highlighted a shift in the All Blacks' selection culture under Dave Rennie, noting an increased edge in camp since the coach took over in January. Rennie has shown a willingness to make personnel changes based on performance, exemplified by the 11 adjustments made for the recent Bledisloe Cup clash. Parsons observed that players now experience a productive nervousness, stating, “I think you've got to take your opportunity, he's not afraid to wield the axe.”

teams.heading: Springboks cement world-leading status by flipping the script on rivals
teams.body: South Africa’s recent 3-1 series victory over New Zealand underscored their evolution, balancing traditional power with newfound attacking intent. While coach Tony Brown’s influence has sought to introduce sharper ball movement, the series ultimately turned on the Springboks’ ability to reassert their dominance in the scrum and maul when challenged. The performance of experienced stalwarts like Malcolm Marx and Eben Etzebeth remains central to Rassie Erasmus’ strategy, ensuring the world champions retain their physicality as their primary trump card.
